arxiv.title: Toward Collective Model Intelligence: Characterizing and Coordinating Models
arxiv.abstract: Independently developed AI models accumulate diverse and complementary capabilities, but a growing model collection does not automatically realize Collective AI. Addressing this gap requires understanding model capabilities with limited evaluation, organizing complementary models to collaborate on diverse tasks, and executing model calls efficiently under resource constraints. We present a systematic approach to pursuing Collective Model Intelligence through three connected components. First, Model Eval constructs evidence-based capability profiles by combining query-level performance estimation with cross-domain prediction, reducing the need for exhaustive evaluation. Second, Mio (Models in One) organizes complementary model candidates and supports task-conditioned, cost-aware selection and collaboration as task requirements evolve. Third, Mos (Model Serving OS) separates model selection from execution and provides endpoint scheduling and shared model deployment and distribution. Experiments show lower capability-estimation errors under limited evaluation. Across nine public benchmarks, Mio 1.0 Lite achieves the highest average score and lowest average cost among compared methods, with per-request costs 73.7-97.5% lower than those of the best-scoring alternatives. A prewarmed shared cache accelerates model-file retrieval by up to 23.3 times. This work lays a foundation for Collective Model Intelligence by characterizing and coordinating the diverse capabilities of an expanding model universe.

arxiv.title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations
arxiv.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used for expensive black-box optimization, yet observation noise makes each evaluation less informative and slows posterior learning. Standard BO learns from costly outcomes gathered during optimization. In many applications, however, low-cost auxiliary data are available beforehand. We introduce Auxiliary-Informed Gaussian Process Bandit (AI-GPB), a variance-reduction method that combines an offline estimate of the auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. Notably, it exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. We establish finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees, including explicit cumulative and simple regret rates for Matérn kernels. Numerical experiments across continuous BO benchmarks with varied landscapes and dimensions show consistent reductions in cumulative and simple regret relative to vanilla GP-UCB, even when within-pair correlation is moderate and the auxiliary mean is estimated from noisy offline data.
arxiv.titleZh: 配对辅助观测下的高斯过程Bandit

arxiv.title: How Does Muon Work in Private Deep Learning? Scalable Differentially Private Training via Orthogonalization
arxiv.abstract: Training deep neural networks requires optimizers that balance computational efficiency with formal data privacy. While orthogonalized update rules, such as the recently introduced Muon optimizer, have shown strong empirical performance and scalability, their behavior under Differential Privacy (DP) is not yet understood. In this paper, we propose DP-Muon, a differentially private variant of the Muon optimizer. By analyzing Muon's orthogonalized updates through the lens of a Linear Minimization Oracle (LMO), we show that the leading effect of per-example clipping is a positive rescaling of the gradient, to which the LMO is blind, so that only a small directional residual controlled by the centered gradient variance enters the optimization error. This yields an $\mathcal O(K^{-1/4})$ convergence rate, up to logarithmic factors, to a clipping-dependent neighborhood at a fixed noise scale and, with noise calibrated to a fixed $(\varepsilon,δ)$ budget, the standard $(\sqrt d/(n\varepsilon))^{1/2}$ privacy--utility bound of DP-SGD, without assuming bounded gradients. Furthermore, we investigate the hyperparameter landscape of DP-Muon and document how the optimal learning rate, momentum, and batch size change under privacy. Empirically, on image classification DP-Muon matches or improves on DP-SGD and DP-Adam, whereas on language modeling the best optimizer depends on the batch size, with DP-Muon best at small batches and DP-Adam best near the privacy-optimal batch size.
arxiv.titleZh: Muon 在隐私深度学习中如何工作？通过正交化实现可扩展的差分隐私训练
arxiv.summaryZh: 分析 Muon 正交化更新在差分隐私（DP）训练下的行为，提出 DP-Muon。借助线性最小化 oracle（LMO）视角，指出逐样本裁剪的主要效应只是梯度的正向缩放，而 LMO 对该缩放不敏感，真正进入优化误差的仅是由中心化梯度方差控制的小幅方向残差。由此在固定噪声下得到 O(K^{-1/4}) 收敛率（至对数因子）到依赖裁剪的邻域，在按固定 (ε,δ) 预算校准噪声时达到 DP-SGD 标准的 (√d/(nε))^{1/2} 隐私—效用界，且无需有界梯度假设。实验显示图像分类上 DP-Muon 持平或优于 DP-SGD 与 DP-Adam，语言建模上最优优化器随 batch size 变化：小 batch 时 DP-Muon 最佳，接近隐私最优 batch size 时 DP-Adam 最佳。

arxiv.title: Can LLM Agents Resolve Service Failures? Simulating Multi-Turn Complaint Handling under Information Asymmetry
arxiv.abstract: LLM agents are widely adopted in service chatbots for rule-guided support and information access, yet emotionally demanding complaint handling still relies heavily on human agents. We introduce ServiceBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark dedicated to complaint handling, with 2,500 scenarios spanning 184 complaint categories and five service industries. We propose Asymmetric Progressive Complaint Simulation (APCS) to simulate realistic complaint handling, together with a justice-based evaluation framework. Our experiments reveal that even capable LLM agents struggle to handle complaints effectively. They lack the ability to proactively gather information and strategically guide conversations toward resolution, often resorting to premature compensation. We further show that targeted post-training with SFT and DPO substantially improves these capabilities, enabling a smaller model to match or surpass much larger models on several outcomes.
arxiv.titleZh: LLM Agent 能否解决服务失败?信息不对称下的多轮投诉处理模拟
arxiv.summaryZh: 针对投诉处理这类高情绪负荷、仍依赖人工的客服场景，构建 ServiceBench:含 2500 个场景、覆盖 184 类投诉与 5 个服务行业，并提出非对称渐进式投诉模拟(APCS)与基于公正感的评测框架。实验显示 LLM Agent 普遍难以主动收集信息、策略性引导对话走向解决，倾向于过早给补偿;用 SFT 与 DPO 做针对性后训练可显著改善这些能力，使小模型在多项结果上追平甚至超过大模型。

arxiv.title: GLOSS-MT: Controllable Low-Resource Machine Translation with an Editable Dictionary
arxiv.abstract: Adapting a pretrained machine translation (MT) model to new terminology usually requires new parallel data and another round of fine-tuning, which is costly for low-resource languages. We ask whether controllability can be added to MT, and the fine-tuning burden reduced, without degrading the pretrained model. GLOSS-MT looks up the source's noun phrases in an offline English-Twi dictionary, replaces every phrase found by its Twi translation in place, and fine-tunes a translation model once to translate these mixed inputs. We apply the same data and pipeline to NLLB-200 (600M, 1.3B, 3.3B), OPUS-MT en-tw and TranslateGemma 4B. On a document-level English-to-Asante Twi benchmark (84 documents, four domains), every fine-tune scores above its pretrained base in chrF2 (+2.85 to +5.48), and the three NLLB fine-tunes are the best open systems (50.12-50.80). A direct controllability test on human-translated Bible passages shows that the three fine-tunes tested write 79-97% of the dictionary terms, and that replacing every dictionary entry by a different term changes the output accordingly (70-97% of the new terms appear) with no retraining. We release the models, data and code.

arxiv.title: fxBench: Evaluating and Understanding Formula Suggestions in Spreadsheets
arxiv.abstract: Spreadsheets are among the most widely used tools for computations, and formulas are their core building blocks. Besides agentic spreadsheet tools, proactive formula suggestions enable significant productivity gains and are now available in popular spreadsheet software (Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets). Such suggestions pose interesting challenges: the right context must be collected and represented for a machine learning model, which must then be able to write a correct formula, in a way that is fast and cheap enough to trigger on every = (or subsequent keystrokes for auto-completion) without taking users out of their editing flow. Surprisingly, there is no public benchmark for formula suggestions on real spreadsheets. In this paper, we therefore (1) introduce fxBench as a manually curated benchmark of 503 formula suggestion tasks based on Sheetpedia, (2) break down the formula suggestion problem into four capabilities (gather context, understand context, understand intent, write formula) that a formula suggestion system requires, and (3) evaluate existing and new approaches to understand bottlenecks in these capabilities that pose interesting research directions. Specifically, we annotate each benchmark with the cells that describe intent to determine the theoretical performance limit of a given context selection strategy, we evaluate performance of small and large models on different representations of context, including a dense format with high theoretical coverage at low token counts, and we fine-tune smaller language models to show that we can learn to understand such dense formats. Additionally, we perform quantitative and qualitative analysis on failure modes to understand bottlenecks in the formula writing capability; the best configuration only achieved 58.8% correct suggestions.
arxiv.titleZh: fxBench:评估与理解电子表格中的公式建议
arxiv.summaryZh: 公式建议是电子表格软件中提升效率的关键功能，但一直缺少基于真实表格的公开基准。为此构建了 fxBench:基于 Sheetpedia 人工整理的 503 个公式建议任务，并把问题拆成收集上下文、理解上下文、理解意图、写出公式四项能力分别评测。基准标注了描述意图的单元格以确定上下文选择策略的理论上限，比较了小模型与大模型在不同上下文表示(含低 token 数、高覆盖率的稠密格式)下的表现，并通过微调小模型证明其能学会理解稠密格式。对失败模式的定量与定性分析显示，最佳配置的正确率仅 58.8%，公式书写能力仍是主要瓶颈。

arxiv.title: Where Natural Language Ends in Agents: Executable Skill Composition with MetaSkill
arxiv.abstract: Agent Skills express open-ended task knowledge in natural language, but composing them requires persistent execution order and upstream-output handoffs. We propose selective formalization at Skill boundaries: coordination relations with stable references and machine-checkable constraints become executable, while substantive task judgments remain within Skills. We introduce MetaSkill, a hybrid representation that preserves complete Skill packages and local instructions while making invocation dependencies and predecessor-text bindings executable through a directed acyclic graph (DAG) runtime. This interface supports explicit coordination without prescribing how each Skill performs its local task. Across 20 multi-Skill artifact tasks and two LLMs, we compare natural-language procedures, prompt-visible graphs, and MetaSkill derived from a common frozen plan per task, using the same designated Skill packages. Additional comparisons evaluate AgentSkillOS with the same available Skill packages as MetaSkill, as well as agent systems using their configured tools. Blinded artifact judgments yield favorable preference point estimates across all reported comparisons, with 95% task-bootstrap intervals excluding parity against Prompt Graph under DeepSeek-V4-Flash and OpenClaw under GLM-5.2. In audited GLM-5.2 execution traces, all planned nodes complete and all declared precedence constraints are satisfied. Together, these findings support MetaSkill as a practical interface for composing open-ended Skills, combining local linguistic flexibility with executable dependencies, explicit predecessor-text bindings, and auditable coordination. Code is available at: https://github.com/TokenRhythm/opensquilla/tree/paper/metaskill-lp4fm-2026

arxiv.titleZh: 自然语言在 Agent 中的边界:用 MetaSkill 实现可执行技能组合
arxiv.summaryZh: Agent Skill 用自然语言表达开放式任务知识，但多技能组合时的执行顺序与上游输出传递缺乏可靠约束。MetaSkill 提出在 Skill 边界做选择性形式化:技能内部的实质性判断仍保留自然语言，而技能间的调用依赖与前驱文本绑定则被形式化为带稳定引用的 DAG，由运行时机器校验执行。在 20 个多技能产物任务、两个 LLM 及 DeepSeek-V4-Flash、GLM-5.2 等对比设置下，盲评偏好点估计均倾向 MetaSkill，部分 95% 任务自助区间排除持平;执行轨迹审计显示计划节点全部完成且前驱约束全部满足。这为可审计的 Agent 技能编排提供了语言灵活性与可执行依赖相结合的接口。

arxiv.title: PV-Decoding: Progressive Verification Decoding with Decode Gating for Diffusion Language Models
arxiv.abstract: Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer an attractive alternative to autoregressive generation by updating multiple tokens in parallel, but their inference efficiency is still limited by the cost of safely committing tentative predictions. In particular, speculative decoding for dLLMs is challenging because speculative tokens within the same diffusion block may depend on one another, making aggressive acceptance prone to error propagation and strict verification computationally expensive. We present PV-Decoding, a confidence-driven speculative decoding framework with progressive verification for block diffusion inference. PV-Decoding partitions masked positions into directly decoded tokens, speculative tokens, and unresolved tokens using two confidence thresholds, and then verifies speculative tokens with progressively stronger policies, including single-batch, dual-batch, and multi-batch verification. This design exposes a practical accuracy--efficiency trade-off: weaker verification minimizes overhead, whereas stronger verification improves acceptance precision and robustness. Experiments on three diffusion language models across GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval show that PV-Decoding reduces sequential model forward passes (MFPs) by 8%--37% relative to confidence-based decoding, while keeping the largest observed accuracy drop to 1.3%. On Dream-7B-Instruct/GSM8K, PV-Decoding (1-batch) and PV-Decoding (2-batch) improve throughput by 7.0%--13.6% under the same hardware budget, whereas PV-Decoding (multi-batch) is slower under the current runtime. These results suggest that confidence-guided speculation with structured verification is a practical path toward efficient and reliable dLLM inference.
arxiv.titleZh: PV-Decoding：面向扩散语言模型、带解码门控的渐进验证解码
arxiv.summaryZh: 针对离散扩散语言模型（dLLM）中，块内投机解码因 token 相互依赖而容易错误传播、严格验证开销大的问题，提出置信度驱动的渐进验证解码框架：用两个置信度阈值把掩码位置划分为直接解码、投机与未解决三类，并对投机 token 施加单批、双批、多批逐级增强的验证策略，形成精度与效率的可调权衡。在三个扩散语言模型与 GSM8K、MBPP、HumanEval 上，顺序前向次数较置信度解码减少 8%–37%，最大精度下降 1.3%；Dream-7B-Instruct/GSM8K 上 1-batch 与 2-batch 配置吞吐提升 7.0%–13.6%。
